excerpt: Watershed is enterprise sustainability software for measuring emissions, filing climate disclosures and cutting carbon. Founded in San Francisco in 2019, it raised a $100M Series C at a $1.8B valuation in 2024.
content:
Watershed is a software platform that helps large companies measure their greenhouse gas emissions, report them to regulators and investors, and reduce them. It pulls in a company's operational and supply-chain data, converts it into emissions figures using its own climate database, and produces audit-ready reports for frameworks such as corporate climate disclosure rules. It also offers tools for engaging suppliers and a marketplace for buying carbon removal and clean power. Its website now describes it as an enterprise sustainability AI platform.

Watershed was founded in 2019 and is based in San Francisco, according to ESG Today. Taylor Francis is a co-founder. In February 2024 the company announced a $100 million Series C led by Greenoaks, with Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Elad Gil, Emerson Collective, Galvanize Climate Solutions and Neo among the existing investors taking part. The round valued Watershed at $1.8 billion, which ESG Today said would make it the most valuable climate software company in the world. Its previous round was a $70 million Series B in 2022. The company said it would use the money for emissions measurement, reporting and decarbonisation products and to expand in the UK and Europe.

ESG Today listed General Mills, Suncorp, Medline, BBVA, Paramount, Spotify and Klarna among its customers, along with four of the six largest US banks. Watershed also acquired CEDA, a greenhouse gas emissions database, and works with partners including KPMG, Accenture and ERM.

Watershed sells to enterprises through demos; it does not publish a price list. This profile is drawn from Watershed's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

profile.summary_short: Enterprise platform to measure emissions, file climate disclosures and decarbonise

gallery.alt: Watershed logo, a blue globe mark beside the word Watershed, on a cream background with soft blue and peach corners

use_cases: Measuring scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas emissions across operations and suppliers
Preparing audit-ready climate disclosures for regulators and investors
Engaging suppliers to collect their emissions data
Buying carbon removal and clean power through its marketplace
Planning and tracking a decarbonisation programme

fit: lead sustainability or finance at a large company facing mandatory climate disclosure
need supplier (scope 3) emissions, not just your own
want measurement, reporting and reduction in one system
not_fit: are a small business that needs a simple, self-serve carbon calculator
want a published price before booking a demo

pricing.intro: Watershed does not publish pricing on its website. You book a demo and get a quote.

plans.name: Watershed platform
plans.detail: Measurement, reporting, supplier engagement and decarbonisation tools

notes: No public pricing page existed when we checked.

pros: Covers measurement, disclosure and reduction in one platform
Large enterprise customer base, including major banks
cons: Built for enterprises rather than small businesses

alternatives.intro: Other carbon accounting and sustainability reporting platforms. We have not compared them hands-on.

items.name: Persefoni
items.what: Carbon accounting and climate disclosure software
items.difference: A like-for-like rival in enterprise carbon accounting and disclosure.

items.name: Sweep
items.what: Carbon and ESG data management platform
items.difference: Positions itself around ESG and EU sustainability reporting as well as carbon.

items.name: Microsoft Sustainability Manager
items.what: Emissions tracking within Microsoft Cloud for Sustainability
items.difference: Fits companies already standardised on Microsoft's cloud.
